contexts.text: They inhere in their opinions so obstinately...
Those of them who obstinately try to emerge...
They obstinately remain in their own dogma.
(The obstinacy of these Spirits.)
Obstinacy. Signified. AC 7300. AC 7412, etc.
Thus by these words is signified obstinacy from the will, and consequently from the delight of doing evil.

As to the obstinacy of those who are in falsities and the derivative evils, and in evils and the derivative falsities, it is to be known that the obstinacy is such that it cannot be described: they never desist, except through grievous punishments... The reason is that the delight of their life is to do evil: this delight they have derived while they lived in the world, especially from this: that they have loved themselves alone... They who are such, because they do not suffer themselves to be led by the Lord, act from their own voluntary proprium... and they who act from (this) act evil from love... and hence they have the delight of doing evil; and, in proportion as they are in this delight, in the same proportion they are in obstinacy. That it is so does not appear in the world... AC 7032:3.
Obstinacy even to the last. Signified.
Obstinacy from the evil of falsity. Signified, Explained.
That they made themselves obstinate. Signified, Explained.
Resistance from the will, and the consequent obstinacy. Signified, Explained.
If they still made themselves obstinate to infest. Signified, Explained.
That they made themselves obstinate. Signified, Explained. AC 7615. AC 7632. AC 7706. AC 8135.
The will can make itself obstinate, but not the understanding.
I observed the obstinacy (of the Sirens), which was so great that I wondered; but their obstinate phantasy cannot be described.
Let him know ... that obstinacy and stubbornness are nothing whatever (as against the punishments there).
Such (Spirits) are... so obstinate that they never desist, unless they are driven away by the Lord; and (then) the febrile heat at once ceases.
See Charles XII here. SE 4742:end. SE 4745.
They throw (this liquor) at Spirits, when they are in their obstinacy and stubbornness.
a. A gulf... whither those are sent, who, on account of stubbornness and obstinacy, cannot be otherwise mastered...
When such (fascinators) approach, they are obstinate and stubborn in the highest degree...
